introduce.title: The Seedance 2.0 prompt formula
introduce.description: A useful prompt behaves like a compact shot brief: identity and setting first, then action and timing, followed by camera, light, sound, style, and constraints.

buttons.title: Try a Prompt in the Generator

items.title: Subject and identity
items.description: Name the subject, wardrobe, materials, expression, and details that must remain consistent across the shot.

items.title: Action and timing
items.description: Describe observable actions in order and use simple time windows such as 0–3s or 3–6s when the sequence matters.

items.title: Camera and composition
items.description: Set shot size, lens feel, camera movement, focus behavior, aspect ratio, and the position of the subject in frame.

items.title: Sound and constraints
items.description: Add dialogue, ambience, music, or silence when needed, plus constraints such as no extra characters or no on-screen text.

benefits.title: Prompt patterns that transfer well
benefits.description: These best Seedance 2.0 prompts and prompt patterns cover common queries such as cinematic prompts, product prompts, image animation, and consistent characters.

items.title: Cinematic story prompt
items.description: Use a beginning, a single camera path, a visible action, and a clear ending pose instead of stacking several unrelated shots.

items.title: Image-to-video prompt
items.description: Tell the model what to preserve from the reference image and what motion, camera change, or environment response to add.

items.title: Product demonstration prompt
items.description: Describe the product surface, hand interaction, lighting reflections, background, and the exact commercial framing you need.

items.title: Character consistency prompt
items.description: Repeat the identity anchors and limit the action to a small number of changes so face, costume, and proportions stay stable.

features.title: Seedance 2.0 prompt examples
features.description: Copy the structure, then replace the subject and action with your own material. The examples are written as directing briefs rather than keyword lists.

items.title: Cinematic tracking shot
items.description: A handheld gimbal follows a cyclist through a rain-wet night market; neon reflections move across the lens, the camera settles on a warm storefront, 16:9, natural motion.

items.title: Image-to-video portrait
items.description: Preserve the person, hairstyle, clothing, and studio background from the reference image. The subject takes one breath, turns toward camera, and the light shifts softly from cool to warm.

items.title: Product close-up
items.description: A matte black camera rotates slowly on a stone table while a narrow key light reveals the dials and texture. Macro lens feel, shallow depth of field, no extra logos, 1:1.

items.title: Vertical social clip
items.description: A baker plates a bright citrus tart in one continuous top-down movement, then the camera tilts to a smiling reaction. Clean counter, quick but natural pacing, 9:16.

items.title: Video-to-video direction
items.description: Use the reference clip for the actor’s blocking and timing, keep the footwork, replace the setting with a sunlit rehearsal studio, and preserve a stable wide shot.

items.title: Audio-aware scene
items.description: A quiet train platform at dawn: distant announcement, rolling wheels, footsteps, and soft wind remain synchronized with a slow lateral camera move.

faq.title: Seedance 2.0 Prompt FAQ
faq.description: Clear answers for the most common Seedance searches and workflows.

items.question: What is the best Seedance 2.0 prompt format?
items.answer: Use subject and identity, environment, action and timing, camera and composition, lighting and color, audio direction, and constraints. Keep the shot internally consistent.

items.question: Can Seedance 2.0 understand prompts in different languages?
items.answer: Language support depends on the selected model and provider. Test a short prompt in the language you need, and use precise visual descriptions instead of relying on a single translated keyword.

items.question: How long should a Seedance prompt be?
items.answer: There is no universal ideal length. Include every decision that affects the shot, but remove adjectives that do not change the image, motion, camera, or sound.

items.question: Can I use a Seedance 2.0 prompt generator?
items.answer: A prompt helper can organize a shot brief, but review every generated instruction for conflicts, unsupported settings, identity rights, and accidental extra actions.

items.question: Where can I find more Seedance prompts?
items.answer: Use the Seedance prompts hub for reusable ideas, then adapt the prompt to the input mode, duration, aspect ratio, and provider settings available to you.
